processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace (applies to all steels including S3).
Promotes uniform composition and microstructure throughout the steel blocks.
Homogenized steel is subjected to step-by-step hot rolling reducing thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.
Samples fabricated using a water jet cutting machine (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA); accurate geometries with minimized thermal distortion. Cylindrical dilatometer specimens ~5x10 mm.

Applied austenitizing temperature for S3 (highest Al, 8.08 wt.%); 1220 °C is the most effective compromise for minimum αp level and maximum austenitizing. Chosen above the MatCalc ferrite-free TA of 1177 °C.

processing_steps.method: rapid cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling rate of 100 K s⁻¹ is sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations and ensure fine bainitic transformation; austempering temperatures selected slightly above the measured Ms (S3 Ms = 258 °C).

Hold at TB = 350 °C to bainitic transformation finish; transformation reached completion at approximately 14,000 s with a 140 s incubation period; a distinctive slow bainite growth period lasted ~1500 s.

structures.overall_structure: Nano-bainitic (nB) microstructure formed by austenitizing S3 at 1220 °C and austempering at 350 °C, comprising bainitic ferrite laths/plates (mixed Type 1 and Type 2 nano-bainite) with blocky/film-like retained austenite (γr) between sheaves, a residual polygonal ferrite (αp) fraction (~8.2%) that could not be eliminated, and cementite-like (Fe,M)xCy carbides near the γr–bainitic ferrite boundaries. Increase of TB to 350 °C raises SD(Lt(t)) indicating a broader range of bainite thicknesses.
structures.number_of_phases: 4 (bainitic ferrite, polygonal ferrite αp, retained austenite γr, (Fe,M)xCy precipitates)

phases_present.morphology: lath/plate bainitic sheaves; mixed Type 1 and Type 2 nano-bainite
phases_present.grain_size: bainite lamellar thickness Lt(t) = 58 nm (SD 23 nm)

phases_present.morphology: occasionally idiomorphic but predominantly allotriomorphic ferrite plates; ferrite plates named by morphology as α or δ nature remains unclear
blocky γr regions between sheaves and film-like γr; partially decomposed sluggish γr in some micro-regions

defects.type: pronounced heterogeneous dislocation distribution / micro-strain partitioning between γr and bainitic ferrite

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: SD(Lt(t)) = 23 nm — widened thickness distribution at TB 350 °C due to coexistence of nB Type 1, nB Type 2 and blocky γr regions

precipitates.type: (Fe,M)xCy cementite-like carbides (M = Si, Mo); rounded morphology inconsistent with spinodal decomposition, indicating nucleation-driven formation
precipitates.distribution: located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries

defect_interactions.interaction_type: carbon partitioning from αp into adjacent austenite
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The low C solubility of pre-existing αp leads to significant C-partitioning into the adjacent austenite (C-enrichment), locally stabilizing the adjacent austenite and inhibiting austenite–bainite transformation by raising the energy barrier around αp plates.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: bainite nucleation/growth stalling at αp–austenite interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Initial nucleation was observed at αp–austenite interfaces, but bainite growth could not propagate and stalled at many sites, producing transformation-free regions requiring significantly longer holding times; the S3 steel retains a noticeable αp fraction even at elevated TA.
At 270 °C the higher average εγ (0.54 %) versus ferritic phase (0.33 %) indicates pronounced dislocation accumulation in γr, forming brittle phase boundaries; (at 350 °C εγ 0.55 % ≈ εα 0.50 %).

interfaces.phase_evolution: For S3 a modified (higher) austenitization approach (1220 °C) was adopted due to the unavoidable presence of αp (~8.2%). αp plates can serve as nucleation sites for bainite but their low C solubility causes C-partitioning and local austenite stabilization, impeding bainite nucleation and growth, leading to partially decomposed sluggish γr in some micro-regions and a distinct slow-growth stage during austempering.
interfaces.interface_notes: The αp facilitates local carbon enrichment and stabilization of surrounding austenite, explaining the slowest bainitic transformation among the studied steels; idiomorphic/allotriomorphic ferrite plates observed by LOM.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All tensile specimens heat-treated using the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle including Bt; Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: PSE (product of strength and elongation) and bainitic transformation time

performance.performance_notes: For S3 at TB 350 °C the PSE was 11,150 MPa·% (UTS 1360 MPa, El 8.2 %). However, at 270 °C (just above Ms) ductility dropped to 2.4 % despite higher UTS (1450 MPa), giving a low PSE of ~3480 MPa·%, confirming a strength–ductility trade-off. The 8.08 wt.% Al design is detrimental to ductility at lower TB; S3 shows the slowest bainitic transformation (Bt 14,000–43,000 s).

characterization_methods.technique: Light optical microscopy (LOM) with ImageJ image analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; etched with 6 % Nital solution; ImageJ (v1.53, NIH); light-optical micrographs at 200×
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 distinct regions analysed after black-and-white contrast in ImageJ
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantitative image analysis of the primary αp volume fraction and spatial distribution; performed only for steel S3 due to its higher polygonal ferrite content
characterization_methods.key_findings: S3 exhibited extensive αp at 1050 °C (area fraction ~14.6 %) and αp persisted even at 1220 °C (area fraction ~8.2 %).

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; gold sputter coating; EDX by Oxford Instruments, Abingdon, UK
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Bainite thickness determined from 10 SEM images per specimen with 100 measurements (10 per image); true lamellar thickness Lt(t) = 2Lt/π stereological correction
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine bainite lamellar thickness and analyse precipitates
characterization_methods.key_findings: Rounded (Fe,M)xCy cementite-like carbides (M = Si, Mo) located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries detected in S3 (Fig. 9 e–k); no micro-void formation.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss SEM with Oxford Instruments EBSD system and software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Accelerating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.2 μm; deformation-free surface by electropolishing and vibratory polishing

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu X-ray tube, 40 kV/40 mA, PIXcel 1D detector (TU Clausthal)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cu Kα radiation; Vγ determined from integrated intensities at (111)γ, (200)γ, (220)γ, (311)γ peaks; ASTM E975-13 guidelines
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and phase micro-strains (εγ, εα) using Eq. (1)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA); cylindrical specimens ~5x10 mm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Heating 10 K s⁻¹ to TA, cooling 100 K s⁻¹; tangent-intersection analysis for Ms; Bt from onset of RLC plateau
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine TA, Ms, incubation and bainitic transformation finish times (Bt)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For S3 (TA 1220 °C): Ms = 258 °C (lowest of the steels); at TB 350 °C, 140 s incubation and Bt ≈ 14,000 s.

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic equilibrium phase calculations and precipitation kinetics / Time–Temperature–Precipitation (TTP) modeling
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc (Version 6.01, rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Austria
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Standard step calculation method; phases considered: fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC; Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy carbide systems; heterogeneous nucleation theory considering only dislocation and grain boundary sites and ortho-equilibrium transformation; volumetric misfit considered; κ-carbides treated as fixed phase fractions (spinodal decomposition).
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Cooling rate 100 K s⁻¹ for TTP diagrams (S3 panel: T_A 1220 °C); austempering lines at TB 350 °C (Bt 14,000 s) and 270 °C (Bt 43,000 s)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: (Fe,M)xCy particles precipitate during cooling between ~700 °C and 1150 °C in S1 and S3 (700–1000 °C for S5); a slight increase of (Fe,M)xCy in S3 compared to S1/S2 attributed to higher Al content, with negligible impact on mechanical properties; MatCalc ferrite-free TA for S3 = 1177 °C, Tcd = 1103 °C, consistent with the residual αp observed experimentally at 1220 °C.

analytical_models.equation_role: Determines Vγ from integrated α/γ XRD intensities combined with the carbide volume fraction Vc (via (1 − Vc) as total bainitic ferrite + γr fraction)

parameters.name: Iα, Iγ
parameters.unit: integrated intensities of α and γ

unmapped_findings: For S3 (TA 1220 °C, TB 350 °C) the bainitic transformation finish time Bt was ~14,000 s with a 140 s incubation period; a distinctive slow bainite growth period lasting nearly 1500 s at TB 350 °C was observed (source blocks b0056, figure_006).
Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for S3 at TA 1220 °C / TB 350 °C was 11,150 MPa·% (UTS 1360 MPa × El 8.2 %) (source block b0063).

Ms of S3 austenitized at 1220 °C was 258 °C, the lowest among the studied steels, consistent with extended κ-carbide dissolution and ferrite retention enabling local carbon partitioning into austenite despite the Ms-raising tendency of its very high Al content (source blocks b0035, b0036, b0056, figure_005).

S3 (highest Al content, 8.08 wt.%) exhibited the slowest bainitic transformation of all studied steels (Bt 14,000–43,000 s depending on austempering temperature), attributed to αp promoting local carbon enrichment and stabilization of surrounding austenite (source blocks b0110, b0056).

No E2₁-type stoichiometric perovskite κ-carbide was directly observed microscopically in the study; residual κ-carbides are presumed to exist as nanoscale, embedded, non-stoichiometric L1₂-type structures due to limited Mn (~1 wt.%) (source block b0085).

The (Fe,M)xCy carbides in S3 showed a slight increase/stoichiometric shift in the TTP curve nose compared to S1 and S2 (attributed to higher Al content), which appears to have a negligible impact on the mechanical properties (source block b0079).
